attempted_claim: Let H be an N x N real-symmetric one-dimensional random band matrix on Z_N with band width W = L^alpha, centered independent entries up to symmetry with standard band variance profile (doubly stochastic band bounds or block-translation invariance + local fullness + irreducibility) and uniform moment bounds. Assume W >> N^{5/6}, and for 1/2 < alpha <= 5/6 consider energies with 2-|E| >> N^{-c_{1,alpha}+epsilon}, c_{1,alpha} = 2alpha-1. Prove via characteristic-flow Dyson Brownian motion loop-hierarchy / zigzag multi-resolvent local laws the optimal entrywise and averaged local laws down to the edge scale, complete L^infty-delocalization max_k ||psi_k||_infty^2 << N^{-1} including edge eigenvectors near +-2 (respectively the gradual bulk-to-edge bound in the intermediate regime), with block/isotropic quantum unique ergodicity and eigenvalue rigidity matching the Hermitian edge exponents of Yang-Yin, asymptotically as N -> infinity with high probability.
decisive_failure: Target edge delocalization theorem for real-symmetric band matrices was not proved: the characteristic-flow loop hierarchy does not close at the edge because the twisted-contraction deterministic calculus and kappa-uniform stability bounds are missing, and finite-N Gaussian numerics test plausibility only. No emergent or fallback claim is made.
